body:
WHAT
A profile is a saved connection (provider, endpoint URL, model, API key, options) stored by the desktop app in ~/.magentra/profiles.json. When the TUI opens a folder that has no credentials yet, it offers the saved profiles in a picker. Choosing one writes the API key into <workspace>/.env and the rest of the connection into <workspace>/.magentra/settings.json, in the same shape the desktop app (the IDE) writes, so the folder looks identical to one connected from the IDE.

WHY
The engine never reads profiles.json; it boots only from the workspace's .env and settings.json. Without this step a terminal user in a fresh folder would have no way to connect, or would produce files the engine or the IDE could not read back.

WHERE
tui/src/profiles.ts — profilesPath(), readProfiles(), environmentKeyVar(), workspaceConnected(ws), keyVarFor(provider), upsertEnvLine(), applyProfile(ws, profile) (writes .env key line and merges provider/baseUrl/model/contextWindow/reasoningEffort/allowInsecureTls into settings.json, deletes apiKeyEnv), readWorkspaceConnection(), clearWorkspaceConnection(), CONNECTION_SETTINGS_KEYS, describeProfile(); caller: tui/src/engine/useEngine.ts — connectThenBoot() and pickProfile(); reference writer being mirrored: app/main.js — applyValidatedConnection(), writeWorkspaceEnvKeys, updateWorkspaceSettings.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. In a temp workspace with no .env, no .magentra/settings.json and MAGENTRA_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/DEEPINFRA_API_KEY unset, workspaceConnected(ws) is false; after applyProfile(ws, {provider:'openai-compat', apiKey:'k', model:'m', baseUrl:'http://h:1/v1'}) it is true.
2. applyProfile for an openai-compat profile writes .env containing exactly one line MAGENTRA_API_KEY=k (and removes a pre-existing DEEPINFRA_API_KEY line), while an anthropic profile writes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=k and leaves DEEPINFRA_API_KEY alone.
3. applyProfile writes settings.json with provider spelled 'openai-compatible' (never 'openai-compat'), model, baseUrl, numeric contextWindow, reasoningEffort, allowInsecureTls only when insecureTls===true and provider is not anthropic, and deletes any existing apiKeyEnv key while preserving unrelated keys already in the file.
4. A keyless profile (apiKey undefined) in a workspace with no .env does not create a .env file at all, but still writes settings.json, and workspaceConnected(ws) then returns true from the settings branch.
5. readProfiles() returns [] for a missing file, for non-array JSON and for entries lacking string id/name; clearWorkspaceConnection(ws) after applyProfile removes every key in CONNECTION_SETTINGS_KEYS and the key line but leaves other .env lines and other settings keys byte-for-byte intact.
